Part A - Creating Vectors and Lists

```{r}
## Question 1: Worker Ages
## a. Create a vector for the worker’s age.
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29,
         35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49,
         50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51,
         35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41,
         48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
age 

## The worker's ages are stored in a vector named `age`. It contains all 50 workers' ages.
```


```{r}
## b. How many data points?

length(age)

## There are 50 data points because the factory has 50 workers.
```

```{r}
## c. Find the minimum and maximum value of workers' ages.

min(age)
max(age)

## The minimum age is 17 years old, while the maximum age is 61 years old.
```

```{r}
## d. Access the 13th to 18th elements and 33rd to 35th elements of workers' ages.

age[c(13:18, 33:35)]

## The code uses indexing to access the 13th to 18th elements and the 33rd to 35th elements of the age vector.
```

```{r}
## e. Access all elements except the 10th, 20th, 30th, and 40th elements.

age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]

## The negative indexing excludes the 10th, 20th, 30th, and 40th elements while displaying the remaining ages.
```

```{r}
## f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.

age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0

age

## The selected elements were changed to zero using indexing and assignment.
```

```{r}
## Question 2: Built-in Dataset - Rivers

## a. Get the length, sum, mean, median, variance, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum of rivers.

data(rivers)

length(rivers)
sum(rivers)
mean(rivers)
median(rivers)
var(rivers)
sd(rivers)
min(rivers)
max(rivers)

## The `rivers` dataset contains 141 observations. The functions calculate the number of elements, total, average, middle value, variance, standard deviation, smallest value, and largest value.
```

```{r}
## b. What is the result? The derived result must be in just one vector name.

rivers_summary <- c(
  length = length(rivers),
  sum = sum(rivers),
  mean = mean(rivers),
  median = median(rivers),
  variance = var(rivers),
  standard_deviation = sd(rivers),
  minimum = min(rivers),
  maximum = max(rivers)
)

rivers_summary

## The results are combined into one named vector called `rivers_summary`. It contains all eight statistical results of the rivers dataset.
```

```{r}
## Question 3: Forbes Ranking

## a. Create vectors according to the table.

celebrity <- c(
  "Celebrity 1",
  "Celebrity 2",
  "Celebrity 3",
  "Celebrity 4",
  "Celebrity 5",
  "Celebrity 6",
  "Celebrity 7",
  "Celebrity 8",
  "Celebrity 9",
  "Celebrity 10",
  "Celebrity 11",
  "Celebrity 12",
  "Celebrity 13",
  "Celebrity 14",
  "J.K. Rowling",
  "Celebrity 16",
  "Celebrity 17",
  "Celebrity 18",
  "Celebrity 19",
  "Celebrity 20",
  "Celebrity 21",
  "Celebrity 22",
  "Celebrity 23",
  "Celebrity 24",
  "Celebrity 25"
)

power_ranking <- 1:25

pay <- rep(NA_real_, 25)

forbes <- data.frame(
  Celebrity = celebrity,
  Power_Ranking = power_ranking,
  Pay = pay
)

forbes
```


```{r}
## b. Modify the power ranking and pay of J.K. Rowling. Change power ranking to 15 and pay to 90.

forbes$Power_Ranking[forbes$Celebrity == "J.K. Rowling"] <- 15

forbes$Pay[forbes$Celebrity == "J.K. Rowling"] <- 90

forbes

## J.K. Rowling's power ranking was changed to 15, and her annual pay was changed to 90. The changes were made using the celebrity's name as the index.
```

```{r}
## Question 4: Vegetables List

vegetables <- list(
  "Carrot",
  "Cabbage",
  "Broccoli",
  "Potato",
  "Spinach",
  "Eggplant",
  "Tomato",
  "Squash",
  "Cauliflower",
  "Cucumber"
)

vegetables
```

```{r}
## a. Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list. What is the result?

vegetables <- append(
  vegetables,
  list("Lettuce", "Okra")
)

vegetables

## Two additional vegetables, lettuce and okra, were added after the last elements of the list. The list now contains 12 vegetables.
```

```{r}
## b. How many data points do you have?

length(vegetables)

## There are 12 data points because the original ten vegetables were increased by two additional vegetables.
```

```{r}
## c. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?

vegetables <- append(
  vegetables,
  list("Bell Pepper", "Onion", "Garlic", "Celery"),
  after = 5
)

vegetables

## Four additional vegetables, bell pepper, onion, garlic, and celery, were inserted after the fifth element of the list.
```

```{r}
## d. How many data points does your vegetable list have?

length(vegetables)

## The vegetable list now contains 16 data points because four more vegetables were added to the previous 12 vegetables.
```
